Context: In this excerpt, original Jamestown colonist Raphe Hamor discusses life in early Jamestown.
Title: Source 4: [Adapted from] a True Discourse of the Present Estate of Virginia (1614)
Author: by Raphe Hamor
Content: We found the colony in a miserable condition upon our arrival there. Fewer than `60` people remained of the nearly `600` who were there `text(ten months)` before. I can now confirm that there is plenty of food, which every man by his own hard work may easily get.

Formerly, when the people were fed out of the common store, some men were happy to avoid labor. To prevent this misbehavior, Sir Thomas Dale has taken a new approach throughout the whole colony. He has assigned to every man in the colony `text(three acres)` of clear ground to raise corn. They are required to pay into the store `text(two)` barrels and a `text(half)` of corn `text(each year)`. This way, our store will be bountifully supplied to maintain `text(three)` or `text(four hundred)` men, whenever they shall be sent to us. The lives of many will be saved.
